g1.label: 1. Rent in the centre is ___ higher than in the suburbs: almost €150 more a month.
g1.why: Considerably is a modifier before a comparative: considerably higher.

g2.label: 2. The new flat is not nearly ___ noisy as the old one.
g2.why: Not nearly as … as means much less than; the adjective stays basic.

g3.label: 3. Of the three flats we saw, this is by far ___ best option for a group.
g3.why: By far goes with a superlative, which takes the: by far the best.

g4.label: 4. The ___ I think about it, the less convinced I am.
g4.why: The + comparative, then the + comparative: the longer I think, the less…

g5.label: 5. Flat B costs twice ___ much as Flat A.
g5.why: Twice as … as shows a multiple: twice as much as.

g6.label: 6. Of the three, Flat A is the ___ convenient for the university.
g6.why: Of three or more, the least + adjective is the lowest degree.

g7.label: 7. Living with flatmates is ___ stressful than I had expected.
g7.why: Less + adjective than compares two things downward: less stressful than.

g8.label: 8. Flat A is in one of the ___ parts of the city.
g8.why: One of the + superlative: one of the quietest parts.

g9.label: 9. Rents are rising ___ than wages, so students are struggling.
g9.why: Rising is a verb, so use the adverb comparative: more quickly.

g10.label: 10. The more flats we saw, ___ we liked the first one.
g10.why: The more…, the more… links two changes that grow together.

g11.label: 11. By the time we reached the second flat, someone had already ___ it.
g11.why: Had already + past participle shows it was taken before we arrived.

g12.label: 12. Would it be possible ___ see Flat B once more before we decide?
g12.why: Would it be possible + to-infinitive is a polite request.
